newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Court awards Reagan Iran-Contra legal fees.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Court awards Reagan Iran-Contra legal fees.

text.p: A U.S. appeals court awarded former President Ronald Reagan $562,111 on Tuesday for legal fees and expenses incurred during the investigation into the Iran-Contra scandal during his presidency.

The three-judge panel made the award after deducting $215,540 from the total amount Reagan had requested for attorneys' fees or expenses during the criminal investigation by independent special prosecutor Lawrence Walsh.

Walsh released his report in January 1994 detailing his lengthy investigation into the scheme by the Reagan White House to sell arms to Iran and divert the profits to the Nicaraguan Contra rebels in the mid-1980s, despite a congressional ban on such military assistance.

His report concluded that "it could not be proved beyond a reasonable doubt that President Reagan knew of the underlying facts of Iran-Contra that were criminal or that he made criminal misrepresentations regarding them."
Under the independent counsel law, an individual who is subject to an investigation but is not charged can be reimbursed by taxpayers for "reasonable" attorneys' fees.

Reagan sought a total of $777,651 in lawyers' fees and expenses from September 1990 through January 1994 while he was a subject of Walsh's investigation. But the appeals court made numerous deductions such as disallowing $111,000 of $335,000 charged by Reagan's attorneys for responding to Walsh's report and $6,340 charged by the lawyers for talking with reporters.
